narrative: Construction and installation governs the finish: 21 of the 21 critical activities and 100% of the remaining critical-path duration fall in this category.
Negative float concentrates in construction and installation (5 activities) - the first place to test whether a delay notice or early warning is due.
Most logic and data defects sit in construction and installation (16 flagged activities), so that part of the programme is the least defensible if the dates are challenged.
root_causes.method: Activity names and WBS paths are matched against a planning taxonomy (design, approvals, procurement, access, weather, enabling, installation, testing). It reads what the work is; it cannot know why it is late - that needs the site records.

items.how: A wait longer than 5 days is work or a hold - model it as a named activity (e.g. 'Await approval') so it can be statused and argued. Links: A1330 → A1340, A1500 → A1510, A1540 → A1550
Add the FS (or FF) link that ties the uncontrolled end - an SS predecessor normally needs a matching FF. Activities: A1320, A1380, A1390, A1430, A1440, A1510, A1520, A1540, A1550
Pair each SS link with an FF from the same predecessor so the successor cannot finish before the work it follows.
Split critical and near-critical ones first, into steps that can be statused weekly. Activities: A1390, A1530, A1580

items.action: Schedule Options → Scheduling logic: Retained Logic
items.how: 4 activities progressed out of sequence. Retained Logic keeps their remaining work behind its predecessors, which is the defensible position; Progress Override silently drops that logic.

items.action: Schedule Options → Define critical activities as: Longest Path
items.how: Longest Path follows logic rather than a float threshold, so constraints and calendars cannot make work look critical.

items.action: Schedule Options → Calculate total float as: Finish Float
items.how: Measure float on activity finishes, which is what drives the completion date, and report it consistently between updates.

items.action: Schedule Options → Make open-ended activities critical: On
items.how: Until the open ends are closed, this exposes them instead of letting them float to the end of the job.

caveats: Metrics are measured on remaining work, except logic density, which counts every activity and link.
Stored total float is what P6 reported at export; the critical path and float-reliability checks also recompute float from the logic alone.
Float suppression, preferential logic and pacing are review candidates identified from patterns - intent can only be established from records.
Liability is a suggestion from the kind of work until someone assigns it; risk allocation depends on the contract, which a P6 export does not contain.
